newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto candidates accuse army of vote-rigging.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto candidates accuse army of vote-rigging.

text.p: Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) on Thursday dragged the army into allegations of rigging votes during the country's recent elections, the state APP news agency reported.
PPP candidates, who suffered a crushing defeat in the February 3 polls, made the charge in speeches at a meeting with Bhutto in the Punjab provincial capital Lahore, APP said.
The news agency, however, did not identify which PPP members made the accusations and the report could not be immediately confirmed.

Bhutto has accused President Farooq Leghari and a caretaker government he installed after sacking her in November of rigging the elections, which gave a landslide victory to the Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party of her rival, former prime minister Nawaz Sharif. The government denies the charge.

The accusations would be the first charges of vote-rigging levelled against the army, which Bhutto had earlier said did not participate in the sacking of her three-year-old government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
No immediate government response was available.
About 250,000 army troops helped the civilian administration maintain peace across the country during polling on February 3.

"Almost without exception, the PPP candidates...complained of pre-polls and polling day rigging and irregularities," APP said. They also said voter turnout was lower than the official count of 35.92 percent of 53.88 million voters.
"The second consistent allegation they made was the presence of army personnel and their influence in coaxing voters to stamp ballot papers against the...(tiger) symbol," APP said.
The tiger is the electoral symbol of the PML.
Army officials were unavailable to comment on the accusations.

Election authorities had given symbols to all political parties, such as the tiger to the PML and arrow to the PPP, for voters, most of whom are illiterate, to place a stamp against the symbol of their favourite candidates on the ballot paper.
The agency quoted the unspecified speakers as accusing troops of virtually controlling polling stations, stamping ballot papers and taking civilian officers who presided over voting into custody.
Bhutto is due to hold a party meeting on Saturday to decide whether to sit in the new National Assembly (lower house) or boycott it.
